intro: One continuous journey from Nursery to Class XII under the Council for the Indian School Certificate Examinations (CISCE), taught in English by teachers who know each child by name.

stages.name: Early Years
stages.summary: A gentle, joyful start where curiosity, language and good habits take root.
points: Play-rich learning in a warm, safe setting
Early literacy and numeracy in English
Holiday homework and activities for every class

stages.name: ICSE
stages.summary: A broad, rigorous curriculum culminating in the ICSE board examination at the end of Class X.
points: Science laboratories for Physics, Chemistry and Biology
15 ICSE batches passed out with meritorious results by the Silver Jubilee

stages.name: ISC
stages.summary: Senior secondary study that prepares students for university, the professions and life.
points: Science subjects with Mathematics or Biology
Computer Science and Physical Education options
Alumni include IITians and doctors serving in India and abroad

iscSubjects.note: Subject options for Class XI as published by the school. [[TO CONFIRM: are Commerce or Humanities streams offered?]]

criteria: Overall performance in the ICSE examination
Character, conduct and behaviour in Classes VIII, IX and X, as assessed by the school
xiAdmission.note: Students who appear for the ICSE examination must apply afresh for Class XI. Students whose presence may prove detrimental to school discipline will not be re-admitted for the ISC course, irrespective of academic results.

pedagogy.title: Holistic, NEP-aligned
pedagogy.text: We have embraced the key principles of the National Education Policy to offer a holistic, future-ready education.

pedagogy.title: Digitally enabled
pedagogy.text: Access to online resources and interactive learning platforms prepares students for a digital age.

pedagogy.title: Parents as partners
pedagogy.text: Regular interactions and workshops help parents understand and support their child’s learning at home.

pedagogy.title: Teachers who keep learning
pedagogy.text: Professional development and in-service programmes keep our teaching methods fresh and improving.

pedagogy.title: Character, health & careers
pedagogy.text: Seminars on character building, health and hygiene, and career counselling are held through the year.

pedagogy.title: A safe, orderly campus
pedagogy.text: Clear discipline policies and safety measures create a calm atmosphere where learning comes first.

coCurricular.title: Sports
coCurricular.text: Football, basketball, kabaddi, kho-kho, cricket and athletics build fitness, teamwork and fair play. CJCians compete at regional and national level.

coCurricular.title: Arts
coCurricular.text: Music, drama, dance and the visual arts nurture creativity, self-expression and a love of culture.

coCurricular.title: Clubs & societies
coCurricular.text: Science, debate and environment clubs encourage enquiry, critical thinking and specialised interests.

coCurricular.title: Competitions
coCurricular.text: Olympiads, spelling bees, science fairs, speech, essay and debate competitions sharpen skills.

coCurricular.title: Exhibitions
coCurricular.text: Students showcase creative, innovative projects and grow in confidence as presenters.

coCurricular.title: Picnics & study tours
coCurricular.text: Educational outings bring curiosity, wonder and experiential learning beyond the classroom.

coCurricular.title: Community service
coCurricular.text: Visits to old-age homes, orphanages, jails, government hospitals and a leprosy colony teach empathy and citizenship.

coCurricular.title: Celebrations
coCurricular.text: Independence Day, Republic Day, Diwali, Christmas, Teachers’ Day, Labour Day and Children’s Day bring the community together.

codeOfDiscipline: Respect all elders and be kind to all.
Love work, and be ready for any kind of work.
Be clean in thoughts, words and deeds.
Do to others what you wish others to do to you.

uniformNote: The school uniform is compulsory. It builds a sense of belonging, unity and, above all, equality among students. Students who do not come in uniform may be sent home at the parents’ risk.
fees: Fees are payable by the 15th of the first month of each quarter. A late fine of ₹20 applies up to the 15th of the following month, and all dues must be cleared before examinations begin. Each year about ten percent of our students, those who are financially weak and eligible, receive a fee concession.
